question: If $$A=\begin{bmatrix}x & 2 & -5 \\ -2 & y & 3 \\ 5 & -3 & z\end{bmatrix}$$ is skew-symmetric, find $x$, $y$ and $z$. Give reason.
explanation:
Diagonal entries of a skew-symmetric matrix
For a skew-symmetric matrix, $A^T=-A$. Hence, for every diagonal entry $a_{ii}$, $$a_{ii}=-a_{ii}\Rightarrow 2a_{ii}=0\Rightarrow a_{ii}=0$$
Application to the given matrix
Therefore, $$x=0,\quad y=0,\quad z=0$$
The off-diagonal entries already occur in opposite pairs $2,-2$, $-5,5$ and $3,-3$.
